title: Upgrade existing Sunshine installations to the security release
head: b6baa706508f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A running Sunshine daemon remains on its vulnerable executable after the package upgrade
leads.consequence: The fix clears unsafe module-loader variables at Sunshine process startup, not dynamically in an already-running process. For a user currently hosting with Sunshine, Omarchy's main pacman update may install the fixed package before this migration (so it skips the version-gated body), or this migration may do the targeted install; neither branch restarts or stops the old process. Sunshine's package post_upgrade only restores capabilities, reloads udev and modprobes, and its user unit restarts on failure only. Omarchy's update-restart step checks kernel/Hyprland and explicit restart markers, not Sunshine. The migration can be marked complete and report success while the active process still executes the vulnerable pre-fix code until a logout/service restart. Check both the packaged unit and any direct Hyprland autostart process, and require or clearly prompt a service restart after installation, including when the preceding system update already installed the fixed package.
leads.triage: sent to Opus (follow-up-1 Q1); confirmed from source, not PR-specific; published as maintainer note with source-only qualifier

leads.summary: New pacman stub fails against the current quattro helper's -- operand separator, breaking the test suite
leads.consequence: When this PR is applied to current quattro (3faafba234e530b0986196b98dc2c38951e7dd6f), omarchy-pkg-present invokes pacman -Q -- sunshine, while the new stub insists its second argument is sunshine. Every presence check returns false. The absent/patched tests pass vacuously, then the vulnerable-version assertion reports 'not ok - vulnerable Sunshine is upgraded' and test/shell and test/all fail. The production pacman accepts --, so this is a test compatibility and coverage defect, not proof that the migration stops upgrading real packages. Fix the -Q stub to accept an optional -- and assert that the vulnerable path was reached.

leads.summary: A patched Sunshine provider is mistaken for an outdated literal Sunshine installation
leads.consequence: Pacman's -Q sunshine falls back to a satisfying provider. Both AUR sunshine-bin and sunshine-git provide sunshine and conflict with the literal package. For a patched sunshine-bin 2026.914.233613-1, -Q sunshine prints 'sunshine-bin 2026.914.233613-1', the prefix removal only strips 'sunshine ', and vercmp of the whole provider line against the minimum is -1. The migration unnecessarily tries unattended pacman -S sunshine>=..., which may request replacing the user's selected provider or fail on the conflict; a nonzero leaves this and every later migration pending and stops omarchy update at the migration step. An installed patched provider should instead be recognized as distinct and skipped (or compared explicitly and upgraded by its own channel), not treated as an old literal Sunshine package. PR #12271's separate helper explicitly skips AUR providers, but combining the two migrations still reaches this defective path.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Finding 2; published. #12271 skip behaviour verified in coordinator/pr-12271.diff

leads.summary: A failed package-presence query silently completes this security migration
leads.consequence: omarchy-pkg-present treats any pacman -Q nonzero, not just 'package not installed', as false. If querying a still-installed vulnerable Sunshine fails due to a local database/read or pacman invocation error, the if body is skipped and the script exits zero without an upgrade or a warning. omarchy-migrate then touches the per-user completion marker, so subsequent migrations/updates for that user never retry this security repair even when pacman recovers. A simulated -Q error with exit 2 and error on stderr yielded migration exit 0 with its error swallowed. Guard the distinction between confirmed absence and a failed probe, and test an error separately from missing package.
leads.triage: sent to Opus (follow-up-1 Q2); real but whole-DB failure only, also blocks -Syu first, common to 12 migrations; dropped

leads.summary: Publishing a fixed PKGBUILD to Git or edge alone does not guarantee a patched stable-channel candidate
leads.location: migrations/1789471023.sh:10; release prerequisite in PR description
leads.consequence: Conditional release hazard: if this migration ships to stable before Sunshine >=2026.914.233613 has been built and promoted into the stable repositories on each supported architecture, existing older Sunshine installations cannot satisfy pacman -S sunshine>=..., leaving the marker pending and stopping omarchy update. The requested prerequisite #458 is closed unmerged, although an automated commit did update the recipe, so its state alone does not establish deployed package availability. Sunshine has no release_ring=fast and normally moves edge to rc to stable only on promotion. Confirm the actual stable sync DB candidate for x86_64 and aarch64 at shipment; order promotion before this migration, or adjust the upgrade path if the fixed build is only in edge.
leads.triage: corroborates and is strengthened by Opus Finding 1 (edge aarch64 missing); DB contents re-verified by coordinator; published

limits: The source PKGBUILD specifies the fixed tag and commit, but I did not inspect live published stable/edge sync databases or carry out a package transaction. H4 is conditional until those database versions are checked.

Sandboxed tests cover head, a synthetic current-quattro overlay, a provider case with fake pacman, a failed presence query, and synthetic merge of #12271. No real Sunshine streaming or live-system upgrade was performed. All sandbox run seals were verified.

Broader topic-word PR searches also surfaced many unrelated PRs; relevant overlapping Sunshine diffs were read, and #12271 was dry-run applied and tested as an explicit overlay. Other source checkouts are not posted comments or peer reviewer outputs.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** for the repository `sunshine` package, the migration does what the description says. Versions older than `2026.914.233613` take the upgrade branch; absent, patched and newer installs are skipped. A failed or ineffective upgrade exits non-zero, so `omarchy-migrate` leaves it pending. The advisory, the minimum version and the upstream tag match, and the PR's test passes on its own head. Three problems remain: the release prerequisite is out of date and no patched aarch64 build is published, AUR Sunshine variants under another name (`sunshine-bin`, `sunshine-git`) can never pass the migration, and the test fails once merged with current `quattro`.

| Real pacman 7.1.0 and `vercmp`, synthetic local database | Result |
|---|---|
| Sunshine absent, or `2026.914.233613-1` installed | exit 0, no `pacman -S` call |
| `vercmp` against `2026.914.233613` | `2026.516.143833-4.1` and `2026.906.222525-1.2` lower; `2026.914.233613-1` equal; `2026.927.202034-1` higher |
| `pacman -T 'sunshine>=2026.914.233613'` | exit 127 for `2026.516.143833-4.1`, exit 0 for `2026.914.233613-1` (matches the test stub) |

### The stated prerequisite is out of date, and aarch64 has no patched build

omarchy-pkgs#458 was closed without merging ("Looks like we already got this one in a daily update"). The same version reached omarchy-pkgs master through the automatic upstream sync (`pkgbuilds/sunshine/PKGBUILD`, `pkgver=2026.914.233613`, `arch=('x86_64' 'aarch64')`), but it is only published for edge x86_64:

| Published `[omarchy]` database, 2026-09-28 | x86_64 | aarch64 |
|---|---|---|
| edge | `2026.914.233613-1` | `2026.516.143833-4.1` |
| rc | `2026.516.143833-4.1` | no Sunshine |
| stable | `2026.516.143833-4.1` | no Sunshine |

Against the edge aarch64 database, `pacman -S --needed --noconfirm 'sunshine>=2026.914.233613'` prints `error: target not found: sunshine>=2026.914.233613` and exits 1, and the migration exits 1 at that step. The edge aarch64 repository already carries an `omarchy-dev` build of the current `quattro` tip, so a merged migration reaches machines running `omarchy-dev` with its next build. Machines on the `omarchy` release package get it only with a later release.

```text
omarchy update
  -> omarchy-update-system-pkgs (-Syu)   no newer Sunshine on edge aarch64
  -> omarchy-migrate
       -> 1789471023.sh: pacman -S 'sunshine>=2026.914.233613'
            error: target not found  -> exit 1
       -> later migrations skipped, marker not written
  -> update stops ("Something went wrong during the update!")
```

**Impact:** aarch64 Sunshine users on edge `omarchy-dev` would hit this failure on every `omarchy update` and every run from the pending-migrations notification until a patched aarch64 build is published. Orphan cleanup, service restarts and post-update hooks after `omarchy-migrate` are skipped as well. The same applies to a development checkout that tracks `quattro` while its pacman channel is stable or rc. For x86_64 rc and stable, the edge to rc to stable promotion described in the omarchy-pkgs README would carry the patched build along with the release; that part is inferred from the documented pipeline, not observed.

**Suggested change:** update the description, since #458 will not be merged. Then either wait until a patched aarch64 Sunshine is published, or let the migration finish without blocking when the configured repositories have no patched build. Because `omarchy update` runs `-Syu` before migrations, a non-blocking version does not lose the upgrade: the first `-Syu` after the build is published upgrades a repository Sunshine anyway, unless it is held in `IgnorePkg`.

### AUR Sunshine variants under another name can never pass the migration

`sunshine-bin` and `sunshine-git` on the AUR declare `provides=('sunshine')` and `conflicts=('sunshine')` without a version. pacman's `-Q` falls back to providers, so with `sunshine-bin 2026.914.233613-1` installed, `pacman -Q -- sunshine` prints `sunshine-bin 2026.914.233613-1`. The `${installed_version#sunshine }` strip does not match that output, and `vercmp 'sunshine-bin 2026.914.233613-1' 2026.914.233613` returns -1, so even a patched or newer AUR package takes the upgrade branch. Then:

- `pacman -S --needed --noconfirm 'sunshine>=…'` picks the repository `sunshine`. `--noconfirm` answers the `Remove sunshine-bin? [y/N]` conflict question with No, and pacman exits 1 with `unresolvable package conflicts detected`. Where no patched build is published, the error is `target not found` instead.
- Even if the transaction succeeded, `pacman -T 'sunshine>=2026.914.233613'` exits 127 for `sunshine-bin`, because an unversioned `provides` does not satisfy a versioned dependency.

**Impact:** a user with `sunshine-bin` or `sunshine-git` gets a migration that fails on every run and stops `omarchy update`, even when their Sunshine is already patched. The pacman conflict error does not explain why.

**Suggested change:** read the package name as well as the version, for example `read -r name installed_version < <(pacman -Q sunshine)`. When `name` is not `sunshine`, print that Sunshine comes from `$name` and has to be updated from its own source, then exit 0 (or apply another deliberate policy). A test case with a provider package would cover it.

### The test fails once merged with current `quattro`

Since #11495 ("Treat command operands as literal values"), `bin/omarchy-pkg-present` on `quattro` runs `pacman -Q -- "$pkg"`. The test's `pacman` stub requires `$2 == "sunshine"` for `-Q`, so on the merge with the current tip `omarchy-pkg-present sunshine` returns false and the migration skips. The test prints `ok - absent, patched, and newer Sunshine installations are unchanged` (passing only because the presence check now fails, so the version check is not exercised) and then fails with `not ok - vulnerable Sunshine is upgraded`. Git reports no conflict, so this only shows up when the tests are run after merging. This is a test-only failure; the migration itself is unaffected by the `--`.

**Suggested change:** accept the separator in the stub. With this line added before `case "$1" in`, the test passes on the merge with the tip:

```bash
[[ ${2:-} != "--" ]] || set -- "$1" "${@:3}"
```

### Notes for maintainers

- **A running Sunshine keeps the old code.** The upstream fix sanitizes the environment and drops privileges once, at the start of `main()`. pacman replaces the binary, but nothing restarts a running process: the package's `post_upgrade` only reapplies `setcap` and reloads udev rules, the user unit only restarts on failure, and `omarchy-update-restart` has no Sunshine case. Omarchy can also start a second copy through the Hyprland autostart line that `omarchy-install-service-sunshine` adds. Every new start runs the patched binary, so the remaining exposure is a process that was already started with a malicious environment. This gap applies to every Sunshine update, and in the normal path `-Syu` upgrades Sunshine before this migration runs. A restart request or notice would therefore only be useful if it does not depend on this migration's upgrade branch, for example `omarchy-state set reboot-required` when Sunshine is installed, patched and running. This is based on source reading only; no running Sunshine was tested.
- **`IgnorePkg = sunshine` is overridden.** `-Syu` respects the hold, but the migration's explicit `pacman -S --noconfirm` answers `sunshine is in IgnorePkg/IgnoreGroup. Install anyway? [Y/n]` with Yes. That may be intended for a security fix, and a line saying so in the migration's output would explain it.
- **Overlapping open PR:** #12271 also adds a Sunshine security-floor migration (`migrations/1789400200.sh`) for the same `2026.914.233613-1` minimum, through a helper that installs the build from edge and skips AUR providers. Its migration sorts before this one, so on x86_64 this PR's migration would then find a patched version and skip. On aarch64, #12271's helper skips when no edge build exists, and this PR's migration still fails. If both merge, two migrations cover the same upgrade.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the PR against its merge base and the current `quattro` tip, plus omarchy-pkgs master and #458, the Sunshine advisory and `v2026.914.233613` source, the AUR `sunshine-bin`/`sunshine-git` metadata and pacman v7.1.0 source. Isolated command-only runs used real pacman 7.1.0 and `vercmp` with synthetic local databases and the published `[omarchy]` sync databases as of 2026-09-28. `-S` runs used `--print` or a synthetic root that stopped before installing anything, with dependency checks skipped (`-dd`) because only the `[omarchy]` database was loaded. The conflict and `IgnorePkg` override results come from runs without `--print`. aarch64 behaviour was checked by pointing x86_64 pacman at the aarch64 database. No real package transaction, sudo, Sunshine process or aarch64 hardware was used, and the full `./test/shell` suite was not run. Published package versions can change after this snapshot.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
